pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an occult ovarian teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of psychotic prodrome progressing to stereotypical orofacial-lingual dyskinesias, autonomic storming with central hypoventilation, the classic "extreme delta brush" pattern on EEG, and the subsequent pelvic ultrasound identifying a mature cystic ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The condition is mediated by pathogenic IgG antibodies targeted directly against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. Ectopic neural tissue expressed within an underlying tumor (most commonly a benign ovarian dermoid cyst/teratoma in young females) breaks self-tolerance, stimulating systemic autoantibody production. These antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and cause cross-linking, internalization, and selective downregulation of cell-surface NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons. This results in the loss of inhibitory tone, causing severe dopaminergic and glutamatergic dysregulation that manifests as psychosis, movement disorders, catastrophic autonomic collapse, and hypoventilation.
